subject: Social Habits
title: Hello and goodbye
objectives: Children will greet people with words or a wave.
content: Saying good morning, greeting the teacher and friends, and saying goodbye with a wave.
teachingActivities: Greet every child by name each morning and expect a response of any kind; model "Good morning" with eye contact; respect that families greet elders in different ways (a wave, a bow, a kneel or a handshake) and never correct a family’s greeting; praise every attempt.
learnerActivities: Greet people with a word or a wave and say goodbye politely.
resources: Pictures of morning, afternoon and evening
assessment: Observe whether each child greets the teacher with a word or gesture and waves goodbye.
expectedOutcomes: Greets the teacher with a word or gesture.

lessons.title: Good morning
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will say or show good morning to the teacher and friends.
successCriteria: Says or signs good morning with support
Looks at the person they greet
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know their names, their teacher and the classroom, and are practising goodbyes.
resources: A picture of the sun rising
lessons.starter: Use a puppet to say "Good morning, friends!" and let the puppet greet each child.
teacherActivities: Show a picture of the sun rising and say "It is morning. We say good morning."
Greet each child by name: "Good morning, Ada."
Sing the good morning song with actions.
learnerActivities: Children look and say good morning.
Child answers with a word or wave.
Child says good morning to the puppet.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a picture of the sun rising and say "It is morning. We say good morning." Children: Children look and say good morning.
Step 2. Teacher: Greet each child by name: "Good morning, Ada." Children: Child answers with a word or wave.
Step 3. Teacher: Sing the good morning song with actions. Children: Children sing and do actions.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children greet the puppet. Children: Child says good morning to the puppet.

practical.title: Good morning circle
practical.safety: Keep the circle small and quiet and sit children away from hazards. Never force a child to speak; accept a wave.

differentiation.support: Greet the child softly and accept a smile.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to greet two friends.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say in the morning?
Who do we say it to?

expectedOutcomes: Looks at the person being greeted
lessons.homeConnection: Greet your child with "Good morning" every day and wait for a reply.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say or show good morning to the teacher and friends" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Good morning, good morning, how are you today?

lessons.title: Greeting my teacher
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will greet their teacher and friends in a polite way.
successCriteria: Greets the teacher at the door
Greets a friend with a word or wave
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know their names, their teacher and the classroom, and are practising goodbyes.
resources: A toy door or a door
lessons.starter: Stand at the door and say "Good morning!" to each child as they enter, with a big smile.
teacherActivities: Show how to greet the teacher with a wave and good morning.
Let children knock on the toy door and greet the teacher inside.
Show how to greet a friend by name.
Talk about how some families greet elders in special ways.
learnerActivities: Children share a greeting from home if they wish.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to greet the teacher with a wave and good morning. Children: Children watch and copy.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children knock on the toy door and greet the teacher inside. Children: Child greets the teacher.
Step 3. Teacher: Show how to greet a friend by name. Children: Child greets a friend.
Step 4. Teacher: Talk about how some families greet elders in special ways. Children: Children share a greeting from home if they wish.

practical.title: Door greeting
practical.safety: Keep the door area clear and supervise closely. Respect each family’s way of greeting and never correct a child’s home greeting.

differentiation.support: Greet together and hold the child’s hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to greet a visitor at the door.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How do you greet your teacher?
How do you greet a friend?

expectedOutcomes: Greets a friend with a word or gesture
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to everyone and say "See you tomorrow."
lessons.homeConnection: Greet family and visitors together and let your child copy.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "greet their teacher and friends in a polite way" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Greeting at different times
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will know that we say good morning, good afternoon and good night at different times.
successCriteria: Says good morning at the start of the day
Says good night at bedtime with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know their names, their teacher and the classroom, and are practising goodbyes.
resources: Pictures of morning, afternoon and night
lessons.starter: Show a picture of the sun and say "Good morning." Show the moon and say "Good night."
teacherActivities: Show each picture and say the greeting.
Match the teddy bear to the time of day.
Pretend to put the teddy to bed and say good night.
learnerActivities: Child places the teddy next to the picture.
Child says good night to the teddy.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each picture and say the greeting. Children: Children say the greeting.
Step 2. Teacher: Match the teddy bear to the time of day. Children: Child places the teddy next to the picture.
Step 3. Teacher: Pretend to put the teddy to bed and say good night. Children: Child says good night to the teddy.
Step 4. Teacher: Sing the greeting song. Children: Children sing with actions.

practical.title: Greeting pictures
steps: Put the three pictures on the floor.
practical.safety: Keep the floor clear of tripping hazards. Be gentle with the teddy.

differentiation.support: Say the greeting together and show the picture.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose the right greeting for a picture.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say in the morning?
What do we say at night?

expectedOutcomes: Says good morning and good night with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say good afternoon.
lessons.homeConnection: Say good morning and good night each day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "know that we say good morning, good afternoon and good night at different times" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Waving goodbye
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will say goodbye politely with a wave.
successCriteria: Says goodbye to the teacher at home time
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know their names, their teacher and the classroom, and are practising goodbyes.
lessons.starter: Sing "Goodbye, goodbye, wave your hand goodbye" and wave to the puppet.
teacherActivities: Show how to wave goodbye and say bye.
Let the toy bus go away and wave goodbye.
Say "Goodbye, teacher" together at the door.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to wave goodbye and say bye. Children: Children copy the wave.
Step 2. Teacher: Let the toy bus go away and wave goodbye. Children: Child waves to the bus.
Step 3. Teacher: Practise goodbyes to friends. Children: Child waves to a friend.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Goodbye, teacher" together at the door. Children: Child waves and says bye.

practical.title: Goodbye practice
steps: Wave goodbye to the toy bus.
practical.safety: Keep the area clear. Stay close to any child who becomes upset.

differentiation.support: Wave together and sing the goodbye song.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say goodbye to every friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do when we go?
Who do you say goodbye to?

lessons.homeConnection: Practise a happy goodbye whenever someone leaves the house.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say goodbye politely with a wave" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Goodbye, goodbye, wave your hand goodbye.

lessons.title: Week 2 greetings check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child greets and says goodbye.
successCriteria: Greets the teacher with a word or gesture
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know their names, their teacher and the classroom, and are practising goodbyes.
lessons.starter: Sing the greeting song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: good morning, door greeting and goodbye.
At each station greet the child and watch the response.
learnerActivities: Child answers with a word or gesture.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: good morning, door greeting and goodbye. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station greet the child and watch the response. Children: Child answers with a word or gesture.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children join the goodbye song.

practical.title: Greeting stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep the floor clear. Accept every form of greeting from the child.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to greet a new friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: greets the teacher; greets a friend; says or waves goodbye; looks at the person being greeted.

questions.question: What do you say in the morning?
What do you do when you go?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 2
Greets and says goodbye with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Share how your child greets and keep practising each day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child greets and says goodbye" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
